case_title: Sheesh Ram and Ors. v. The State of Rajasthan
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: land dispute and an earlier murder case between the appellants' side and the victim's family
statutory_provisions: IPC s.148, s.302 r/w s.149, s.307 r/w s.149 (as charged/convicted at trial); on final appeal, IPC s.302 r/w s.34 and s.307 r/w s.34 for the appellants
weapon: Axes, a sword, a dhariya and lathis
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured eyewitness PW-5 and three corroborating eyewitnesses); medical evidence (post-mortem/doctor's testimony on cause of death)
aggravating_circumstances: Brutal attack: fatal head injury with axe blows after the victim had fallen, and a second victim attacked with multiple weapons
trial_court_outcome: All accused convicted under IPC ss.148, 302 r/w 149 and 307 r/w 149; sentence for the appellants not stated in the trial court's outcome
high_court_outcome: Four accused acquitted; the appellants' convictions altered to IPC s.302 r/w s.34 and s.307 r/w s.34 with life imprisonment and fines
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 r/w s.34 (murder of the victim); IPC s.307 r/w s.34 (attempt to murder of the second victim)
neutral_facts: The victim's father and two of his sons were standing by a road when a tractor carrying several men stopped beside them. The men got down and, armed with axes, a sword, a dhariya and lathis, encircled the father and sons. The father and one son ran towards the village. The victim ran in another direction but was chased. One assailant caught hold of him and struck his head with an axe; after he fell, another assailant struck him again with an axe, and a third hit his right hand with a dhariya. According to the doctor who gave evidence, the victim died from haemorrhage and shock caused by the head injury, which damaged the brain and the carotid artery in the neck. The victim's brother was also attacked: he was caught, struck on the left temple with a dhariya and behind the ear with an axe, and hit on the face with a lathi, after which he became unconscious. He received four incised wounds and a fracture of the left parietal bone. The assailants left believing both were dead. The injured brother gave a detailed account of the incident. Two other eyewitnesses, who were related to him, described the same events and were found to be consistent on the main prosecution case. The parties had a prior dispute over land and an earlier murder. The accused examined defence witnesses.
physical_harm: Victim died from haemorrhage and shock due to head injury (injury to brain and carotid artery in neck); second victim suffered four incised wounds, a fracture of the left parietal bone, and unconsciousness
motive: Prior enmity: the appellants' brother Kamal was murdered and the victim's father and some witnesses were facing trial for that murder, giving the appellants a strong motive; the Court did not accept that this led to false implication
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of the injured eyewitness PW-5 Bhagwan Singh, corroborated by PW-2, PW-3 and PW-4; medical evidence on cause of death from PW-12; eyewitness evidence accepted on the main prosecution case
witness_credibility: PW-5 (injured eyewitness) found trustworthy and his evidence not dented on cross-examination; interested (related) witnesses scrutinised with caution and accepted; exaggeration regarding acquitted accused disbelieved but severable from the main case; defence witnesses not believed
trial_duration: offence: 04/02/1991; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 29.05.2003; Supreme Court: January 29, 2014
legal_representation: Accused/appellants: P.C. Agarwala, Ambuj Agarwal, Chander Shekhar Ashri. State: S.S. Shamshery, AAG, and Milind Kumar
investigation_status: FIR registered on complaint; charge-sheets laid against the accused (appellants' charge-sheet dated 3/2/1993); case committed and tried in Sessions Court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.148, 302/149, 307/149 IPC. High Court: four accused acquitted; appellants convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 and s.307 r/w s.34 IPC. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, convictions upheld
prosecution_argument: Eyewitness evidence is consistent and reliable; PW-2 and PW-4 are independent; falsus in uno principle does not apply in India so the credible remainder can be relied on (relying on Rizan); enough credible evidence to prove the case
defence_argument: Witnesses exaggerated and implicated the acquitted accused, so the evidence is risky to rely on; falsus in uno falsus in omnibus should apply; eyewitnesses appear tutored and interested; complainant not examined; false implication due to long-standing enmity cannot be ruled out
legal_principle_applied: Evidence of interested witnesses is not always suspect and must be scrutinised with caution; exaggeration severable if it does not change the prosecution story; falsus in uno is only a rule of caution, and the grain can be separated from the chaff
precedent_relied_upon: Balaka Singh v. State of Punjab (1975) 4 SCC 511; Rizan & Anr. v. State of Chhattisgarh (2003) 2 SCC 661
judicial_aggravating_factors: Brutal manner of the killing as noted by the Court
